Kuwait’s Sweeping Tariff Hike Disrupts Imports, Raises Prices Across Sectors

KUWAIT CITY — Kuwaiti businesses and consumers are feeling the immediate effects of a nationwide tariff increase on imported goods, implemented last week as part of the government’s bid to strengthen domestic industries. The new measures, which raise import duties by an average of 20% across a broad range of products, remain in effect as officials evaluate their economic impact.

The tariffs were introduced abruptly, with the Ministry of Finance citing the need to “support local manufacturing and ensure economic resilience.” However, the move has caught many importers off guard. “We are already seeing delays at customs and confusion over the new rates,” said Khaled Al-Mutairi, chairman of the Kuwait Importers Association. “There’s uncertainty in every sector, from electronics to foodstuffs.”

Supermarkets and retailers, such as the widely-used Al-Sabah Markets chain, have reported price increases on many imported goods, including packaged foods, electronics, and household items. “Customers are asking why the price of basic essentials like rice and cooking oil have gone up overnight,” said Reem Al-Ajmi, a store manager in Salmiya.

Economists warn that the tariff hike could stoke inflation. “Kuwait is heavily reliant on imported goods,” explained Dr. Sara Al-Fahad, an economist at Gulf Policy Research. “A broad tariff increase will inevitably push up costs for consumers and businesses alike.”

The Chamber of Commerce has called for urgent dialogue with the government, urging a review of the policy. Customs officials, meanwhile, say they are working overtime to process new declarations and ensure compliance. As the measure continues, business leaders and consumers alike await clarity on when — or if — the tariffs might be eased.
